s.t:
We see the semiconductor industry as a realm of possibility. We see opportunity. We see the profound impact that our graphene solutions will have in transforming the industry. We invite you to join us in driving change with our fundamentally human-centered approach, uniting bright minds around a shared vision.

The vision is: Prove to everybody that you can make a fundamental change. Prove with your knowledge and skills how things can be done differently. Together, we can change the paradigm of how the world connects
About our technology
The semiconductor industry’s growing demand for more powerful chips with higher bandwidth and lower power finds its solution in our technology. We connect chips to high-throughput, low-delay computing networks.

The key lies in harnessing the physical properties of graphene to combine electronic computing with photonic communication, allowing countless chips to interact almost as if they were one. Our graphene photonic innovation increases computing power and efficiency to a new order of magnitude
In short, we connect chips to create powerful and energy-efficient networks, overcoming connectivity limitations in the semiconductor industry. We deliver the graphene solution

At Black Semiconductor, we are building the foundation of next-generation chip manufacturing with Fab One , our first production facility. To support this, we are looking for an Industriemeister Electrical Engineering / Master Electrician (f/m/d) who is not only experienced in hands-on electrical work, but also eager to take ownership of complex facility infrastructure in a high-tech industrial environment.
In this role, you will play a key part in the founding team establishing the electrical and building infrastructure of Fab One. You will be directly involved in the setup, commissioning, and ongoing development of electrical distribution systems and building services.
Beyond traditional electrical engineering tasks, you will progressively develop expertise in building automation and facility control systems (FMCS), with external training provided to support your growth in this area.
If you enjoy understanding complex technical systems, working in a structured and analytical way, and contributing to the build-up of a highly advanced industrial environment, this role offers a strong long-term growth path.
To join our team, you should be excited to
Take on a key first-hire role in the setup and commissioning of facility infrastructure for Fab One, directly contributing to the development of building automation (FMCS) systems. This includes supporting commissioning activities, system integration, troubleshooting, and gradually building expertise in control logic and HMI systems.
Oversee electrical works performed by external contractors, ensuring safety, quality, and timely execution on site.
Diagnose faults in complex installations and control circuits, and review/approve electrical documentation, including schematics, wiring diagrams, and as-built drawings.
Manage electrical compliance, inspections, and testing in coordination with relevant authorities, ensuring accurate technical documentation and certification.
Oversee procurement and quality assurance of electrical materials and contribute to technical design reviews for both new installations and retrofit projects.
Work closely with facility managers, project engineers, and external contractors to deliver reliable, compliant installations on time.

Successfully completed Meister qualification in Electrical Engineering (Industriemeister Electrical Engineering or Master Electrician, certified by a German Chamber of Commerce or equivalent)
Strong hands-on background in electrical engineering with deep experience in industrial or commercial environments
Extensive practical experience in installation, maintenance, commissioning, or troubleshooting of electrical systems
Solid knowledge of relevant German standards and regulations
Ability to read and interpret electrical schematics, single-line diagrams, and wiring plans
Structured, analytical, and solution-oriented approach to technical problem-solving and fault diagnosis
Initial exposure to building automation (FMCS/BMS), industrial controls, or similar systems is a strong advantage and will be further developed in this role.
Excellent communication skills in German (both written and spoken); professional working proficiency in English is considered a plus.
Our work culture
People Over Processes. At Black Semiconductor, flexibility is key—we ensure work adapts to life, not the other way around. We champion work-life harmony, where careers are meaningful and enriching. Our processes are human-centric, allowing you to focus on what matters
Let’s grow together. Your potential is our priority. We provide the autonomy to make a lasting impact and nurture your growth through a culture of continuous learning. We invest in your journey for professional and personal development
Your Health and Future Matter. Your well-being is paramount. We offer a comprehensive benefits package with outstanding insurance, pension and virtual stock options for your mental, physical, and financial health. Your peace of mind is our priority - in the present and future
We Live Openness. Collaboration and inclusivity are the cornerstones of our culture. We practice openness, fostering trust and respect. Individuality is our collective strength, fueling innovation and driving us forward
We connect chips – and people. We encourage qualified individuals from any background to apply. We foster an inclusive and supportive work environment that values collaboration, innovation, and growth. Join our team and be part of an organization dedicated to making a difference in the industry

Here at The Exploration Company, we are developing, producing, and operating Nyx, a modular and reusable space orbital vehicle that can eventually be refuelled in orbit and that can carry cargo - and potentially humans in the longer run.
To support this ambitious goal, we are seeking an Electrical Test Technician to join our Electrical Integration & Test Team in Munich. You will be responsible for the assembly, integration, maintenance, and modification of electrical test systems used throughout the development, verification, and validation of spacecraft subsystems and avionics equipment.
You will play a key role in building and maintaining custom test racks, integrating commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) and custom-designed hardware, and supporting engineers during test campaigns. Working closely with electrical, avionics, and system engineers, you will help ensure our test infrastructure meets the highest standards of quality, reliability, and safety.

s.h: In your role as Electrical Test Technician, you will
s.t:
Assemble, wire, and integrate electrical test racks and ground support equipment
Perform wiring and interconnections between COTS equipment and custom-designed hardware
Manufacture, route, label, and install electrical harnesses and cables according to engineering documentation
Interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and technical drawings to perform integration and troubleshooting activities
Support electrical integration, verification, and test campaigns across multiple projects
Perform inspections, modifications, and repairs on electrical assemblies and test equipment
Assist in the installation, replacement, and rework of electronic components on PCBs when required
Execute continuity, insulation, and basic electrical verification tests on assemblies and harnesses
Maintain accurate documentation of wiring modifications, test setups, and configuration changes
Support troubleshooting and root-cause investigations on electrical and test systems

s.h: You and your team will be in charge of
s.t:
Building and maintaining reliable electrical test infrastructures for spacecraft development and qualification activities
Integrating a wide variety of electrical equipment, including power supplies, measurement devices, automation components, and custom electronics
Ensuring all rack assemblies and wiring installations comply with internal standards and safety requirements
Supporting engineers during test setup preparation, execution, and troubleshooting activities
Contributing to the continuous improvement of test equipment, assembly processes, and documentation practices
Maintaining high levels of workmanship, quality, and configuration control across all electrical integration activities
Ensuring electrical installations are safe, maintainable, and suitable for demanding aerospace test environments

Technical diploma, vocational qualification, or equivalent experience in Electrical Engineering, Electronics, Mechatronics, Industrial Automation, or a related field
Proven hands-on experience in electrical assembly, wiring, and integration activities
Ability to read, interpret, and work from electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and technical documentation
Experience assembling and wiring electrical cabinets, racks, or industrial control systems
Knowledge of cable and wire selection principles, including preliminary conductor sizing based on electrical loads and installation constraints
Familiarity with common industrial automation components such as relays, contactors, circuit breakers, terminal blocks, sensors, power supplies, and I/O modules
Experience using standard electrical test equipment, including multimeters, oscilloscopes, power supplies, and continuity testers
Strong troubleshooting skills and a structured, methodical approach to problem-solving
High attention to detail and commitment to quality workmanship
Fluent in English, with excellent written and verbal communication skills
Ability to collaborate effectively with multidisciplinary engineering teams in a fast-paced environment
Nice-to-Have Skills
Experience with aerospace, automotive, railway, or other highly regulated industries
Experience performing PCB assembly, component replacement, soldering, and electronic rework
Familiarity with low-voltage DC power distribution systems
Knowledge of cable harness manufacturing and connector assembly standards
Experience working with custom-built test equipment and Hardware-in-the-Loop (HiL) environments
Ability to design rack front panels and front-end layouts for custom test systems
Familiarity with CAD tools for electrical or mechanical design documentation
Understanding of configuration management and documentation control processes
Why you should join us!
What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is:
We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind
We’re Open and Collaborative - we are transparent about risks and obstacles, so that we can cooperate to overcome them
We have a lot of Fun - we refuel our energy knowing we are democratising space. It’s a wonderful and rare opportunity, are YOU up for the challenge?
We'd love to hear from you if you wish to be a part of our journey. Please submit your CV now for immediate consideration and we will be in touch shortly.

Here at The Exploration Company, we are developing, producing, and operating Nyx, a modular and reusable space orbital vehicle that can eventually be refuelled in orbit and that can carry cargo - and potentially humans in the longer run.
We want you as a talented and experienced Electrician to help us in our mission by developing Hardware-in-the-Loop platforms for our Future Projects. You will be part of the Future Systems team, reporting to the Principal Engineer of the project and working closely with the other engineering disciplines.

As an Electrician-HIL, your role will evolve as our testing capabilities grow. Initially, your day-to-day responsibilities will include, but not be limited to:
Design, build and wire HIL test benches, racks, and electrical harnessing for spaceflight and ground test systems
Assemble and integrate electrical infrastructure for HIL environments, including power distribution, signal routing, grounding and shielding
Support setup and operation of HIL test benches, integrating hardware with simulators, instrumentation and test equipment
Diagnose and troubleshoot signal integrity issues, intermittent connections, grounding problems, and EMI/EMC-related effects
Maintain, modify and repair test equipment wiring, connectors, harnesses and supporting electrical infrastructure
Maintain accurate wiring schematics, cable lists, test logs, and configuration documentation
Collaborate with HIL engineers, System Engineers and software teams to support test readiness and failure investigations
Contribute to continuous improvement of HIL hardware design, build process and safety practices
What we would love to see from you
In the role as Electrician - HiL ideally, you will bring the following experience and skills:
Technical diploma or bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, mechatronics, or related field
3+ years of hands-on electrical work, preferably in aerospace or high-reliability/safety-critical environments
Demonstrated experience assembling and wiring HiL test benches, racks, or complex test setups
Strong ability to interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, pin‑outs, and harness drawings
Familiarity with aerospace or industrial standards (e.g., ECSS, MIL‑STD, IPC, or equivalent)
Practical experience in cable and harness fabrication , including crimping, soldering, heat‑shrinking, and connector assembly
Proficiency with electrical and electronic test equipment , such as multimeters, power supplies, oscilloscopes, signal generators, and harness testers
Solid understanding of EMI/EMC best practices , grounding concepts, and shielding technique
Experience with spacecraft avionics, GSE, or propulsion test systems is a plus
High attention to detail, strong workmanship standards, and a safety‑first mindset
Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively within a multidisciplinary team
Skills and Behaviors
Strong oral and written communication skills
Strong analysis and problem-solving skills
Strong organizing and prioritization of tasks
Positive and flexible attitude to get the job done
Ability to communicate at all levels of the business
Demonstrates behaviours consistent with The Exploration Company’s core values of Mission, Vision, Integrity, Excellence and Teamwork

s.t:
You will perform non-supervisory work and directing the work of three or more mechanics of the trade, and/or any additional helpers, workers, and apprentices assigned.
You will provide general direction on how to perform the work and demonstrate initiative to get the job started.
You will check the progress of jobs and resolve delays when possible.

Although a specific length of time and experience is not required for most trade and labor occupations, you must show through experience and training that you possess the quality level of knowledge and skill necessary to perform the duties of the position at the level for which you are applying.

Qualification requirements emphasis is on quality of experience, not necessarily the length of time. Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the job elements and screen out listed below.

This job has a screen-out element which will be used to determine minimum eligibility for this job. Applicants who do not receive a minimum of two points on the screen-out element(s) will be found ineligible. The Screen-out Element for this position is: Ability to Lead or Supervise.

Applicants must meet the requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Job Qualification Handbook for Trades and Labor Occupations.

Additional qualification information can be found at: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/federal-wage-system-qualifications/#url=List-of-Approved-Job-Elements Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

Installs, modifies, inspects, tests and repairs electrical distribution lines, secondary lines, substations, transformers, breakers, regulators, insulators, lightning arrestors, switches, fuses and similar equipment.
Works on underground and overhead primary distribution systems of up to 115,000 volts.
Troubleshoots distribution systems and equipment using devices such as voltmeters, ohmmeters, phase meters, meggers, underground cable locators and thermal imaging cameras.
Checks voltage of secondary terminals, and makes repairs to defective, loose, or corroded connections.
Works from building plans, drawings, and manuals to plan, layout, determine wire, fixture and equipment type and size, balance the load, and ensure the proper and safe operating of electrical lines, circuits, systems, equipment and controls.
Performs work associated with installing, maintaining, troubleshooting, repairing, and calibrating complex electronic equipment such as, protective relays, reclosures, tap changers, regulators, battery chargers, and circuit breakers.
Operates boom crane devices at various outdoor locations where maneuverability is restricted due to close proximity of high voltage lines and equipment and accuracy is critical.
Periodically inspects all transformers, lines, streetlights, substations, manholes, underground cables, and arresters.

Work requires bending, stooping, climbing, and standing for long periods. Coordination of eyes, hands, legs, and body is needed in installing, repairing, and testing electrical equipment in confined spaces such as manholes and overhead structures.

Working Conditions - Works outside most of the time, subject to extremes of weather conditions, which could result in mandatory 24-hour emergency call, and in close proximity to high voltage lines and equipment. Work requires extensive pole climbing with some work in underground facilities.

Subject to death or serious injury by contact with high voltage lines, broken bones in falls from poles, strains from awkward positions, and less serious cuts and bruises when handling tools and materials.

May be required to work in contaminated areas, exposed to hazardous chemicals and toxic fumes requiring the wearing of uncomfortable protective devices including respirators and impermeable rubber suits.

Engine & Powerplant Maintenance
Remove, install, and replace engine components and assemblies following approved procedures.
Inspect, troubleshoot, and repair engine ancillary equipment including fuel systems, ignition systems, oil systems, and cooling systems.
Conduct engine ground runs and operational tests to verify proper function. Maintain and repair engine mounts, cowlings, exhaust systems, and air induction systems.
Monitor engine parameters and diagnose mechanical and performance issues. Handle fuel system maintenance includes pumps, filters, lines, and tanks.
Electrical Systems
Install, inspect, test, adjust, and repair aircraft electrical systems including power generation, distribution, batteries, and wiring.
Test electrical components and assemblies using circuit testers, oscilloscopes, voltmeters, and multimeters.
Assemble and install electrical components using hand tools and soldering equipment.
Perform system functional tests. Repair or replace defective electrical wiring, connectors, and electronic components.
Documentation & Compliance
Maintain accurate maintenance logs, work orders, and aircraft records in compliance with aviation regulations.
Ensure compliance with FAA/EASA airworthiness directives and service bulletins.
Safety & Quality Assurance
Follow all aviation safety procedures, regulations, and best practices.
Conduct pre-flight and post-maintenance inspections.
Identify and report safety hazards or airworthiness discrepancies.
Ensure all work meets quality standards and regulatory requirements.

Working independently and responsibly. Perform tasks as described above.
Compliance according to ANAVIA’ employment contract, compliance with company’ safety instructions and employee’ safety requirements, compliance with employers’ quality manual, work instructions and corresponding process specifications and instructions.
Your profile

Education: Technical diploma in aircraft maintenance, electrical systems, or mechanical related field. Avionics training or certification or engine-specific training certifications a plus. EASA Part-66 license a plus.
Experience: Minimum 3-5 years of hands-on experience maintaining aircraft electrical systems, engines, and mechanical components. Proven experience working on turbine or piston aircraft engines. Experience with aircraft electrical troubleshooting and avionics systems. Familiarity with helicopter systems (rotorcraft, turboshaft engines) is highly desirable. Experience in aerospace, aviation, or rotorcraft maintenance environments a plus.
Skills: Working knowledge of aircraft electrical systems, power generation, and distribution. Proficiency in reading and interpreting electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and technical drawings. Solid mechanical aptitude with expertise in engine systems and fuel systems. Proficient use of electrical test equipment.
Skilled in using hand tools, power tools, torque wrenches, precision measuring instruments. Familiar with aircraft maintenance and technical documentation.
Safety and Regulatory: Commitment to safety, quality, and continuous improvement. Strong attention to detail with systematic and methodical approach to troubleshooting. Understanding of fuel system safety procedures and handling practices. Working knowledge of relevant aviation regulations a plus.
Physical: Capable of standing, walking, bending, kneeling, stooping, and working in awkward positions for extended periods. Manual dexterity and fine motor skills for precision work with small components and soldering. Visual acuity to inspect components, read technical documents, and identify defects. Hearing ability sufficient to detect abnormal sounds during engine runs and equipment operation.
Communication: Effective communication skills for coordinating with team members, engineers, and management. Ability to work independently with minimal supervision. Self-motivated and able to manage multiple tasks and priorities.
Language: Good language skills in English (oral and written). German desirable.

### Devenez membre de notre équipe, mettez la main à la pâte et façonnez avec nous l'avenir de l'énergie ! Nous sommes un prestataire de services énergétiques intégré du canton d'Argovie. Nous atteignons nos objectifs grâce à des collaborateurs compétents qui s'engagent activement dans le processus d'amélioration continue. Nous offrons des espaces de liberté, nous nous faisons confiance et nous nous traitons avec respect. ###
Vos tâches
* Vous planifiez, organisez et réalisez de manière autonome des formations pour les apprentis électriciens de réseau et garantissez une haute qualité de formation.
* Dans les cours interentreprises, vous assumez le rôle de formateur/trice et d'instructeur/trice et transmettez les contenus de manière pratique.
* Vous coordonnez les cours de répétition et de formation continue pour adultes et apprentis, de la planification à la mise en œuvre, et développez continuellement l'offre.
* Lors des cours sur les opérations de commutation et les travaux sous tension, vous apportez votre expertise ciblée, soutenez la réalisation et assurez un déroulement sécurisé.
* Vous élaborez, entretenez et optimisez continuellement les documents de cours et de formation.
* Vous participez activement aux comités spécialisés, apportez votre expérience pratique et donnez des impulsions pour le développement de la formation.
* Vous accomplissez les tâches administratives dans le domaine de la formation de manière structurée et efficace, assurant ainsi un déroulement sans accroc.
* La sécurité au travail est votre conviction profonde, tant dans la formation que dans la participation à l'analyse des incidents et à la mise en œuvre des mesures.
Votre profil
* Votre bagage de formation comprend une formation achevée en tant qu'électricien/ne de réseau ainsi qu'une formation continue en tant que maître électricien de réseau ou technicien/ne HF.
* Vous possédez de préférence le certificat SVEB de formateur/trice et l'utilisez efficacement en pratique. Une formation en pédagogie des adultes et en sécurité au travail est un atout supplémentaire.
*
* Une expérience professionnelle de plusieurs années dans le secteur d'une entreprise de fourniture d'énergie vous aide à transmettre les contenus de manière pratique et adaptée au groupe cible.
* Vous vous sentez à l'aise dans la formation d'apprentis et/ou d'adultes et prenez volontiers la direction technique.
* Grâce à votre habileté didactique, vous concevez des cours variés, compréhensibles et précis.
* Une présence assurée, une communication forte et des compétences en modération vous caractérisent - même dans des situations exigeantes.
* Vous travaillez de manière structurée, autonome et avec un haut niveau d'exigence en matière de qualité, de sécurité et de responsabilité ; de bonnes connaissances en allemand ainsi que le permis de conduire catégorie B complètent votre profil.

À propos de nous
AEW Energie AG est une entreprise indépendante du canton d'Argovie. Avec une fourniture d'énergie sûre et respectueuse du climat, nous contribuons de manière significative à l'attractivité du site et à la qualité de vie dans la région.

Nous nous engageons dans la production d'électricité et de chaleur/froid ainsi qu'en tant qu'opérateur de réseau leader et fournisseur pour nos clients. Pour la production d'électricité, nous nous concentrons sur l'énergie hydraulique ainsi que sur l'énergie solaire et éolienne.
